_llm_instructions: Fill out the 'project_title' and 'date_prepared' properties, and the 'value' property of each field below, based on the available project context. Refer to parameters.md for the shared project variables. Name the model version, the group affected, and the threshold that triggers action, rather than recording a category; a governance plan that says 'encrypted', 'minimised' and 'monitored' describes an intention and not a system, and the difference only becomes visible when something goes wrong and no one can say what was in force.

f01_Assessment_Objective.section: Purpose and Scope of the Assessment
f01_Assessment_Objective.label: Assessment Objective
f01_Assessment_Objective.guidance: What decision this assessment is being made to support, and what decision it is not. A readiness assessment with no stated decision attached is a score, and a score nobody needs is the one most often abandoned.

f02_Assessment_Scope.section: Purpose and Scope of the Assessment
f02_Assessment_Scope.label: Assessment Scope
f02_Assessment_Scope.guidance: Which systems, processes and teams are in scope, and which are excluded. Excluding something is legitimate; excluding it without writing it down is what lets it reappear as a dependency in month four.

f03_Assessment_Method.section: Purpose and Scope of the Assessment
f03_Assessment_Method.label: Assessment Method
f03_Assessment_Method.guidance: How each dimension was assessed: instrumented measurement, walkthrough, interview, or self-declaration. Self-declaration is legitimate and must be labelled, because an unlabelled self-declaration is indistinguishable from a measurement and is trusted accordingly.

f04_Assessor_and_Date.section: Purpose and Scope of the Assessment
f04_Assessor_and_Date.label: Assessor and Date
f04_Assessor_and_Date.guidance: Who performed it, on what date, and against which version of the systems. A readiness figure without a date is a figure that decays silently.

f05_Evidence_Basis.section: Purpose and Scope of the Assessment
f05_Evidence_Basis.label: Evidence Basis
f05_Evidence_Basis.guidance: What the scores rest on, and where the evidence sits. A score whose source cannot be retrieved cannot be defended when it is challenged, which is the only time its accuracy matters.

f06_Data_Availability.label: Data Availability
f06_Data_Availability.guidance: Whether the data the use case requires exists, at the volume and coverage needed. Availability is not the same as permission, and the gap between them is the most common reason a data-ready organisation is not an AI-ready one.

f07_Data_Quality.label: Data Quality
f07_Data_Quality.guidance: Completeness, consistency, timeliness and validity, each with the measurement used. "Good quality" is a conclusion; a completeness figure against a defined field list is an input to one.

f08_Data_Lineage_and_Documentation.label: Data Lineage and Documentation
f08_Data_Lineage_and_Documentation.guidance: Whether it can be traced to its origin and meaning. Lineage is what makes a defective output diagnosable rather than merely wrong, and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact.

f09_Labelling_and_Ground_Truth.label: Labelling and Ground Truth
f09_Labelling_and_Ground_Truth.guidance: Whether labelled examples exist for the intended purpose, in sufficient quantity and quality. Where they do not, say so, because labelling is a programme of work with a cost and a duration, and treating it as a task hides both.

f10_Data_Governance_and_Access.label: Data Governance and Access
f10_Data_Governance_and_Access.guidance: Who may access what, under what controls, and whether that is settled. Access rights settled late are the usual cause of a launch delay that no one predicted, and they are settled late because they involve people outside the team.

f11_Compute_and_Capacity.label: Compute and Capacity
f11_Compute_and_Capacity.guidance: Whether the capacity required for training and inference exists, and at what cost. Cost per unit of work is the figure that decides whether the use case is viable at volume, and it is not known until the volume is.

f12_Platform_and_Tooling.label: Platform and Tooling
f12_Platform_and_Tooling.guidance: MLOps, versioning, experiment tracking, deployment and monitoring. The tooling question is not whether a notebook runs but whether a model can be reproduced, rolled back, and monitored in production, since those are the operations a team inherits.

f13_Integration.label: Integration
f13_Integration.guidance: Whether the system connects to the surrounding estate, and at what quality. Integration is where readiness assessments are optimistic, because a proof of concept connects to nothing and a production system must connect to everything.

f14_Security_and_Resilience.label: Security and Resilience
f14_Security_and_Resilience.guidance: The controls in force for AI workloads, and what happens when the system is unavailable. A system whose fallback is manual reverts to a process that was automated because it was unworkable by hand.

f15_Scalability.label: Scalability
f15_Scalability.guidance: Whether performance and cost hold as volume grows. A model that is accurate and unaffordable at ten times the volume is a prototype, and the assessment is where that is cheapest to discover.

f16_Team_Composition.label: Team Composition
f16_Team_Composition.guidance: Who is on the team, and which of the required roles are unfilled. List the gaps by role rather than by competence, because a gap named by competence has no owner and a gap named by role has a vacancy.

f17_AI_Skills.label: AI Skills
f17_AI_Skills.guidance: The specific capabilities present, at what level: building, evaluating, deploying, and operating. These are different skills and a team strong in the first may be unable to do the third, which is where readiness usually fails.

f18_Domain_Expertise.label: Domain Expertise
f18_Domain_Expertise.guidance: Whether the team includes people who know the domain well enough to judge an output is wrong. Without them the team can measure performance and not interpret it, and those are not separable.

f19_Capacity_and_Availability.label: Capacity and Availability
f19_Capacity_and_Availability.guidance: Whether the people named are actually available at the required fraction, given other commitments. A team rostered at half time and a team absent are the same fact expressed differently.

f20_Capability_Building.label: Capability Building
f20_Capability_Building.guidance: How gaps will be closed: hire, train, partner, or buy. These have different lead times and the lead time is the constraint, not the preference.

f21_Leadership_Sponsorship.label: Leadership Sponsorship
f21_Leadership_Sponsorship.guidance: Whether there is a sponsor who will fund the consequences as well as the work. Sponsorship that ends at approval has funded a demonstration, and the difference surfaces at the first decision the system makes that somebody disputes.

f22_Operating_Model.label: Operating Model
f22_Operating_Model.guidance: Who runs the system in production, and under which service commitment. An operating model decided at go-live is an operating model negotiated in an incident.

f23_Change_and_Adoption.label: Change and Adoption
f23_Change_and_Adoption.guidance: Who must change their work, what they gain, and what they lose. A system that makes someone's judgement redundant will not be adopted regardless of its accuracy, and adoption is not a communications problem.

f24_Procurement_and_Contracting.label: Procurement and Contracting
f24_Procurement_and_Contracting.guidance: Whether the contracts permit the intended use, and what they permit the supplier to do with the data. These are the obligations that cannot be renegotiated after the data has been shared.

f25_Risk_Appetite.label: Risk Appetite
f25_Risk_Appetite.guidance: What level of failure the organisation will accept, and who accepts it on its behalf. A risk appetite that is never stated becomes, by default, zero tolerance, which is not a position anyone chose.

f26_Dimension_Scores.label: Dimension Scores
f26_Dimension_Scores.guidance: The score for each dimension, with the scale used stated. A score without its scale cannot be compared with a later assessment, and the comparison is the only reason to take the first one.

f27_Weighted_Overall_Score.label: Weighted Overall Score
f27_Weighted_Overall_Score.guidance: The aggregate, with the weights and their justification. An unweighted average treats a dimension the business does not depend on as equal to one it cannot operate without.

f28_Blocking_Gaps.label: Blocking Gaps
f28_Blocking_Gaps.guidance: The gaps that prevent proceeding, as distinct from those that slow it. This distinction is the assessment's actual output, and a form that records a single list cannot make it.

f29_Recommended_Route.label: Recommended Route
f29_Recommended_Route.guidance: Proceed, proceed with conditions, remediate, or do not proceed, and the condition attached. The route without its conditions is an opinion; the conditions are what can be tracked and closed.

f30_Remediation_Plan.label: Remediation Plan
f30_Remediation_Plan.guidance: What will be done, by whom, by when, and what it costs. A gap with no owner and no date is not a gap in the plan, it is a gap in the plan's assumptions.

f31_Reassessment_Trigger.label: Reassessment Trigger
f31_Reassessment_Trigger.guidance: What would cause the assessment to be repeated. Readiness decays as staff move and data drifts, and an assessment with no expiry is treated as current indefinitely.
